messages.subject: simsim with ordinal categorical data
parts:
I am trying to use simsem to simulate a model whose parameters are estimated with lavaan. sim just hangs and appears to do nothing. I'm thinking that I may have made a mistake.

      mydata.fit <- cfa(lavaanModel, data=mydata, estimator="WLSMV", ordered=names(mydata))
     mydataModel <- model.lavaan(mydata.fit, std=TRUE)
     sim(100,n=160, mydataModel, lavaanfun="cfa",ordered=names(mydata))

Every variable in mydata is categorical with 3 ordered categories. The last line causes the computer to go off and execute something endlessly.

I noticed that the results of model.lavaan didn't seem to give information about the cut-points that define the ordinal variables, so perhaps that is where the problem is. I'm hoping there is a way of doing this without explictly typing out the population model with estimated parameters, since that would be very tedious in this case. It's quite a big model.


Thanks.

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: simsim with ordinal categorical data
parts:
Hi Gella,

I am sorry for the late reply. The model.lavaan does not work with categorical data. We have not integrated the categorical features in the matrix framework yet. It is actually in our plan.

The model.lavaan function actually can be avoided. First, the fixed-factor method of scale identification is used to make the loadings being on the standardized scales (i.e., both factor and indicator variances are 1). Then, the following script should work:

library(psych)
library(simsem)
dat <- iqitems

iq.model <- '
matrix =~ matrix.45 + matrix.46 + matrix.47 + matrix.55
rotate =~ rotate.3 + rotate.4 + rotate.6 + rotate.8
'
fit <- cfa(iq.model, data=dat, estimator="WLSMV", ordered=names(dat)[9:16], std.lv=TRUE)

simout <- sim(3, n=160, model=iq.model, generate=fit, lavaanfun="cfa", estimator="WLSMV", ordered=names(dat)[9:16])
summary(simout)

I will try to get the matrix framework and model.lavaan function work with categorical items soon.Thank you for your feedback.

Best,
Sunthud
